reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that lineup construction in GPPs must balance ownership risk with scoring leverage. The 5–10% ownership bucket offers optimal risk-adjusted returns due to reduced field overlap. Salary efficiency correlations show that paying down on positions with weak predictive value (like D/ST) is advantageous. Stack leverage dynamics reveal that tight ends should be placed in game stacks rather than flex slots to maximize top-100 usage. These primitives form a dual framework: one for risk mitigation (ownership zones) and one for scoring maximization (salary efficiency and stack dynamics). Failure modes include overexposure to high-ownership players (dead zone) and misallocation of salary toward low-efficiency positions. The interplay between these operators defines the structural space of viable lineups.
